verdict.rationale: Runpod's Pod docs say you can connect to a deployed Pod through JupyterLab or through VS Code/Cursor for local IDE integration. Official templates ship with JupyterLab preconfigured, so it is ready immediately after deploy. The community remarks about a "locked down" environment concern third-party remote-kernel and tunneling setups, not Runpod's own Jupyter or IDE access, and are hedged. missing for 10: explicit documentation of a one-click/one-step connect flow for VS Code/Cursor, step-by-step IDE connection details, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can open Jupyter or connect my IDE (VS Code/Cursor) to the instance in one step

citations.quote: Once deployed, you can connect to your Pod through SSH for command-line access, web proxy for exposed web services, JupyterLab for data science workflows, or VS Code/Cursor for local IDE integration.
Access your Pod via SSH, JupyterLab, or VS Code.
Instead of installing PyTorch, configuring JupyterLab, and setting up all dependencies yourself, you can select an official Runpod PyTorch template and have everything ready to go instantly.
